pr_title: Fix Issue#6173: Update WmiRequest constructor to wstring from BSTR
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to osquery! -->

This PR fixes https://github.com/osquery/osquery/issues/6173. Now, BSTRs are allocated from wstrings, and freed after use. Previously, wide-character strings were being C-casted as BSTR and then provided to WMI objects: Providing wide-character strings as BSTRs to functions and methods requiring BSTRs is undefined.

At the moment, there are other source files calling WmiRequest both with valid BSTRs and wstrings. Both cases will work without any side-effect.  I will make these cases consistent in a separate PR.

issue_context.title: WmiRequest explicit constructor's second parameter should be std::wstring and not BSTR
issue_context.body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to osquery! -->

# Bug report

<!--
Please follow this template.
Before submitting an issue search for duplicates.
-->

### What operating system and version are you using?
N/A

<!--
You can run the command bellow. Paste result within a code block.

osqueryi --line "SELECT version, build, platform FROM os_version;"
-->

### What version of osquery are you using?
master branch
<!--
You can run the line bellow. Paste the result within a code block.

osqueryi --line "SELECT version from osquery_info;"
-->

### What steps did you take to reproduce the issue?
Looking at PR https://github.com/osquery/osquery/pull/5246

### What did you expect to see?
The second argument to this explicit constructor should be an std::wstring instead of BSTR.

### What did you see instead?
BSTR is a special structure for strings in windows, and needs to be allocated with SysAllocString and freed with SysFreeString. Casting a std::wstring to BSTR is incorrect and will lead to unexpected errors. Better approach would be to construct a BSTR from the wstring parameter, and free it after use.
comments: I see several instances of the pattern `(BSTR)L"WQL"` in the code base. How are these working given the data structure expectation for a `BSTR`?

> I see several instances of the pattern `(BSTR)L"WQL"` in the code base. How are these working given the data structure expectation for a `BSTR`?

Passing in wchar_t strings to methods/functions that explicitly request BSTRs results in undefined behavior. These are different data-types.

Here is one reference: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/atl-mfc-shared/allocating-and-releasing-memory-for-a-bstr?view=vs-2019

review_comments: If the code returns early here then `language_str` is leaked, we will need to call `SysFreeString(language_str)`
Good catch! Maybe later we can use _bstr_t to auto-destruct these.
